title: Florissant Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Florissant wells have a 280-foot median depth, with typical finished-well costs of $24,200-$40,000.
h1: What Florissant Wells Really Cost and Produce
intro_html:
Buying land near Florissant means dealing with mountain bedrock, not a uniform shallow aquifer. Records within 5 miles show a median well depth of 280 feet and a median reported pump yield of 5.0 gallons per minute. Those figures are useful for planning, but they do not guarantee what a new well will find on a particular lot.

Most permitted wells here serve domestic or household use, and the aquifer names point mainly to unnamed fractured bedrock. Before buying, compare nearby well permits, ask for construction and pumping records, and have a driller price the actual access and site conditions.

sections.heading: Florissant well depth follows the fractured mountain rock
sections.html:
Florissant wells are commonly drilled into fractured granite, gneiss, or other crystalline bedrock. The local median depth is 280 feet, while the middle half runs from 151 to 400 feet. That range is the better starting point for a drilling budget than the median alone.

Depth varies sharply from lot to lot. 42% of recorded wells fall between 300 and 600 feet, and 7% are deeper than 600 feet. The deepest recorded well is 1,100 feet. A bid based only on a neighboring shallow well can be misleading, especially where fractures do not continue across a property.

For a buyer, ask the driller to explain the assumed footage, casing and grout approach, and what happens financially if the hole must continue beyond the estimate.

sections.heading: A Florissant well may make usable water without making much
sections.html:
The median reported pump yield near Florissant is 5.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half between 1.5 and 9.0 gallons per minute. That is a workable planning range for many household systems, but it is not a promise of continuous flow from a new hole.

Yield records are spread across the range: 14% report less than 1 gallon per minute, 33% report 1 to 5 gallons per minute, and 49% report 5 to 15 gallons per minute. Only 4% report more than 15 gallons per minute.

Low-yield homes often depend on storage tanks and careful peak-use planning. Have the driller discuss a pumping test, storage capacity, recovery time, and whether the proposed household use fits the permit.

sections.heading: Water levels vary, and the older record is thin
sections.html:
Among wells reporting a static water level, the median depth to water is 100 feet, with the middle half from 70 to 145 feet. That measurement is not the same as well depth: a 280-foot well may encounter static water considerably above its bottom.

The decade series does not show a simple steady decline. Median water level was 88 feet below the surface in the 1970s, 45 feet in the 1980s, 85 feet in the 2010s, and 115 feet in the 2020s. Only 215 wells report a static water level, so treat the pattern as a local comparison tool rather than proof of a basin-wide trend.

Nearby records from Divide, Lake George, Midland, or Woodland Park may help, but a site-specific test remains more useful.

sections.heading: Permit history shows a long-running domestic well area
sections.html:
Colorado DWR records contain 3,773 permitted wells within the mapped area, with 2,563 recorded as constructed. Most are domestic or household wells, making up 94% of the use mix. Stock wells account for 4%, monitoring wells for 1%, and irrigation is recorded at 0%.

Permit activity was highest in the 1990s, with 993 permits, after 692 in the 1980s and 546 in the 1970s. The record includes 207 permits from the 2020s, and the newest permit year is 2025.

The most active drillers in these records are Mountain Well Improvement LLC, Woods Drilling Inc., and RMPD, Ltd. DBA Rocky Mtn Pump & Drilling. A permit history is useful background, but verify the current license, scope, and references before hiring anyone.

sections.heading: Florissant drilling cost starts with footage
sections.html:
Local ground conditions are fractured mountain bedrock, described in the cost model as granite and gneiss. The typical drilling rate is $65 to $100 per foot. At the local median depth of 280 feet, the drilled hole models to about $18,200 to $28,000.

That is not the complete water-system price. A finished well including the pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at about $24,200 to $40,000. Access, difficult setup, casing, grouting, water storage, and unusual site work can affect the actual proposal.

Use the range to compare bids on equal terms. Ask what footage is included, which components are allowances, how unsuccessful drilling is handled, and whether the price includes testing and the equipment needed for a low-yield fractured-rock well.

sections.heading: Mines, PFAS sites, and septic layout deserve attention
sections.html:
Mapped environmental records within about 10 miles include 3 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 34 historic mine features, and 9 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. A map hit does not automatically mean a parcel's well is contaminated, but it is a reason to check the exact location, groundwater direction, and available sampling results.

Low yield and dry holes are separate risks from water quality. Fractured bedrock can produce a useful well on one lot and a poor result nearby. Test existing water for the contaminants relevant to the site, and use a qualified laboratory.

Before building, confirm well access for a rig, septic setbacks and soil suitability, electrical routing, storage needs, and the legal permitted use. Keep the well, septic system, and replacement areas workable on the site plan.

sections.heading: What to do before buying a Florissant lot
sections.html:
Start with the DWR permit record for the parcel and nearby wells. Look for total depth, reported yield, static water level, construction details, and the aquifer description. The local records are dominated by unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers: 3,656 wells are listed that way, with 65 Fractured Crystalline wells and 29 Fractured Granite wells. No Denver Basin aquifer wells are recorded.

Then get a driller to inspect access and provide a written depth and completion allowance. A buyer should understand the plan if the hole reaches low-producing fractures, requires more footage, or needs storage to make household use practical.

For a building project, coordinate the well, septic design, driveway, trenching, and house location before closing. In an over-appropriated basin, confirm whether an augmentation plan or other water-right requirement applies to the intended use.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Florissant, Colorado?
faq.a: The median recorded well depth near Florissant is 280 feet. The middle half runs from 151 to 400 feet, but 42% are between 300 and 600 feet, and the deepest record is 1,100 feet. Fractured granite and gneiss make nearby well depths an imperfect guide for a new lot.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Florissant?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $65 to $100 per foot. At the 280-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $18,200 to $28,000. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at $24,200 to $40,000. Access and difficult bedrock can change the actual bid.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Florissant?
faq.a: The median reported yield is 5.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 1.5 to 9.0 gallons per minute. However, 14% of reported wells produce less than 1 gallon per minute. Ask about pumping tests, recovery, and storage because fractured-bedrock wells can vary substantially between nearby properties.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Florissant?
faq.a: The permit records do not establish that every well is safe to drink. Within about 10 miles, mapped records include 3 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 34 historic mine features, and 9 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Test the specific well through a qualified laboratory and investigate any nearby environmental site before relying on the water.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a lot with a well in Florissant?
faq.a: Review the DWR permit, construction depth, yield, static water level, and legal use. Local records show a 100-foot median static water level and mostly domestic wells. Have a driller inspect rig access and the bedrock risk, and coordinate well, septic, driveway, and building locations. Confirm any augmentation-plan or other water-right requirement for the intended use.
